body:
Nicotine pouches are easy to use once you know the basics, but small habits make a real difference to comfort, hygiene and how the product feels. This guide walks through each step for first-time users, explains where to place a pouch, how long to keep it in, how to dispose of it, what to expect in the first few uses, what to do if you feel unwell, how to avoid common mistakes, how to be considerate of others and how pouches fit into daily life. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and this is general information, not medical advice. Follow the instructions on the can.

## Before you start
Make sure you are 21 or older and that nicotine products are allowed where you are. Read the instructions on the can, check the strength and make sure the pouch looks intact. Do not use a pouch that is torn, dried out or damaged. If you are new to nicotine, choose a lower strength; see [strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/).

## Step 1: wash your hands
Clean hands keep the pouch hygienic, and avoid transferring dirt to your mouth. If you cannot wash, use a hand sanitizer and let it dry before you handle the pouch, because sanitizer can taste unpleasant and transfer to the pouch.

## Step 2: open the can and take a pouch
Open the can and take out one pouch with clean fingers. Close the lid firmly straight away, to keep the remaining pouches fresh. Some cans have a slot in the lid for used pouches. Do not take more than one at a time.

## Step 3: place the pouch
Put the pouch between your upper lip and gum, usually on one side. Some people prefer the lower lip. Position it where it is comfortable, and avoid pressing it too hard. Try different spots over several uses, and use the one that feels best. Move the pouch to a different spot from time to time, because leaving it in the same place can cause irritation.

## Step 4: wait
You may feel a tingling or warmth as nicotine releases, and the flavor builds over a few minutes. Keep it in for the time in the instructions, generally up to about 30 minutes. You do not need to move it, chew it or suck on it. If it feels too strong, remove it early. If the flavor fades, the pouch may be spent.

## Step 5: remove and dispose
Take the pouch out and throw it in a bin. Do not flush it or leave it on the ground. Many cans have a built-in disposal slot for used pouches. Wash your hands afterward. Used pouches still contain nicotine, so keep them away from children and pets. See [storing pouches](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/).

## Tips for comfort
- **Do not chew or swallow the pouch.**
- **Drink water** if your mouth feels dry.
- **Do not use more than one pouch at a time** unless the instructions allow it.
- **Start with a lower strength;** see [strengths explained](/blog/nicotine-pouch-strengths-explained/).
- **Rotate the spot** where you place it.
- **Avoid eating or drinking acidic drinks** while the pouch is in, because they can reduce absorption and affect taste. Many people wait before drinking coffee, juice or soda.

## What you might notice
A light tingle, warmth or mild burning in the area is common, especially with stronger or minty pouches. Some people notice extra saliva, a slight numbness or a metallic taste. Irritation on the gum can occur if the pouch is left in the same place for long. If irritation continues, stop using it and speak to a healthcare professional.

## If you feel unwell
Remove the pouch and rinse your mouth. If you feel faint, dizzy, sick or have a fast heartbeat, stop using and sit down, drink water and seek advice if it continues. These feelings can mean the strength is too high for you. Nicotine is addictive; this is not medical advice. If you think a child or pet has swallowed a pouch, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 or your vet immediately.

## How often and how many
Follow your own judgment and the instructions. Using more pouches means taking in more nicotine, and nicotine is addictive. If you notice that your use is creeping up, think about why, and consider speaking to a healthcare professional for support.

## Etiquette and travel
Be considerate: dispose of used pouches properly, avoid using them in meetings or around people who may be bothered and check the rules of the place you are in. See [pouch etiquette and travel](/blog/nicotine-pouch-etiquette-and-travel/).

## Storage
Keep the can closed, cool and dry, and away from children and pets. See [how to store pouches](/blog/how-to-store-nicotine-pouches/).

## Common mistakes
- **Using a high strength first.** Start low.
- **Chewing the pouch.** It is not meant to be chewed.
- **Leaving it in too long.** Follow the instructions.
- **Dropping used pouches on the ground.** Dispose of them in a bin.
- **Leaving cans open.** They dry out.
- **Sharing with someone under 21.** Never.

## A worked example
You buy a can of 6 mg mint pouches. You wash your hands, open the can and take one pouch. You place it under your upper lip on the left. After a minute you feel a tingle, and the mint flavor builds. After about 20 minutes the flavor fades. You remove the pouch and put it in the slot in the lid. You wash your hands. The next time you use one, you place it on the right side, to give the first side a rest.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I talk with a pouch in?
Yes. Most people find pouches discreet and easy to talk with.

### Can I eat or drink with a pouch in?
It is better to avoid it, as eating and drinking can affect absorption and the pouch. Many people take it out first.

### Will a pouch stain my teeth?
We make no claims. Ask your dentist for advice about oral care.

### How do I stop the pouch moving?
Place it firmly and keep your lips relaxed. Smaller pouches tend to stay put.

### What if I accidentally swallow a pouch?
Stay calm, drink water and seek advice if you feel unwell. Contact Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 if in doubt.

## Shop
Browse [nicotine pouches](/shop/nic-pouches/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Troubleshooting common issues
### The pouch slips around
Try a different position, and place it firmly under the lip. A slimmer pouch may stay in place better. Keep your lips relaxed.

### The flavor is too intense
Choose a milder flavor, or a lower cooling rating. Remove the pouch early if you need to.

### My gum feels sore
Rotate the position, give the area a rest and stop if it persists. Speak to a healthcare professional if you are concerned.

### The pouch feels dry
Drier pouches take longer to release flavor. Give it a minute, or try a moister product.

### I forget to remove it
Set a reminder at first. After a few uses, you will learn the timing.

## A short daily routine
Keep a can in a pocket, close the lid each time, use a pouch when you choose to, dispose of it in a bin and wash your hands. Check the date on the can each week. A simple routine prevents most issues and keeps your use under your own control.

## Related reading
See [pouch flavors](/blog/nicotine-pouch-flavors-guide/) to choose what to try next, and [how many pouches are in a can](/blog/how-many-pouches-in-a-can-and-how-long-it-lasts/) to plan how many cans you need.

## Frequently asked questions about daily use
### How many pouches a day is normal?
There is no single answer, and we cannot give medical advice. Use as directed, and be aware that nicotine is addictive. If your use is rising, consider speaking to a healthcare professional.

### Can I use a pouch before sleep?
Many people avoid it, because nicotine is a stimulant. Follow your own judgment, and remove the pouch before you sleep.

### What if the pouch tears?
Remove it and rinse your mouth. Do not swallow the contents, and use a new pouch if you want to continue.

### Can I use pouches during exercise?
Some people prefer not to. If you feel unwell, stop. Follow your own judgment and the instructions on the can.

### Does a pouch affect my breath?
Flavors can leave a minty or fruity taste, and some people notice a change. Rinsing with water helps.

## Building good habits from the start
Habits formed in the first weeks tend to stick. Decide in advance when you will use a pouch and when you will not, keep a regular place for the can, remember to wash your hands and always dispose of used pouches properly. If you notice that you are reaching for a pouch automatically, pause and ask whether you want one. A little awareness keeps your use deliberate. If you ever feel that your use is controlling you, speak to a healthcare professional, because support is available.

## What to do next
Choose a flavor you like, with a low strength, try one can and see how it fits your routine. See [pouch flavors](/blog/nicotine-pouch-flavors-guide/) and [pouch brands compared](/blog/nicotine-pouch-brands-compared/) for ideas on what to try. Browse [nicotine pouches](/shop/nic-pouches/) when you are ready.
